assessments.summary: The static rct4 encoding, elementary variable counts, line-enumeration logic, weighted-at-most-two translation, and half-turn/quarter-turn sublemmas are substantially correct. However, the declared package is not fully established: its exhaustive rotational classification omits rotations of orders other than two and four, and its exact constraint counts, certificate-check results, and bounded solver-run history lack trusted execution evidence.
scopeQualifications: The model is sound and complete only within the stated rct4 class; it does not cover general half-turn, reflection-symmetric, or asymmetric configurations.
The elementary counts of 1444 off-diagonal orbit variables, 38 diagonal-pair variables, and 154 selected points are analytically supported.
The contribution supplies neither a 154-point certificate nor an infeasibility proof and therefore does not change the stated interval 152 <= D(77) <= 154.
Even if the bounded searches occurred as reported, their UNKNOWN/timeout outcomes would provide no evidence of nonexistence.
The rotation lemma correctly excludes half-turn symmetry at size 153, quarter-turn symmetry at sizes 153 and 154, and locates any half-turn center for a 154-point set at (38,38).

Neither declared reference is mathematically necessary: c5e8096d942d57228bb4fed00f7617fb6b43af9f is motivational/provenance material, while the decoding and model arguments associated with dfc0cc40d41105292a119840dcdbe6f22860cf43 are supplied within the subject.
evidenceIssues: The assertion that half-turn symmetry about (38,38) is the only rotational symmetry available above 152 points is unproved because rotations of orders other than two and four are not excluded; consequently the claim that every 153-point set has no rotational symmetry is also unresolved.
The exact figure of 388,148 distinct constraints and analogous calibration counts require execution or independent reproduction; results.json alone does not attest them.
Claims that all five known certificates pass exhaustive determinant, structural, and model checks lack terminal attestations or independently verified computation.
The provenance claim that the certificate lines were reproduced from the external database is unsupported by a content-addressed snapshot, though it is not needed for the static model argument.
External python-sat cardinality generation and OR-Tools/CaDiCaL behavior are not attested by included clauses, logs, transcripts, generated CNF bytes, or trusted execution records.

The reported solver runs are not fully reproducible: the displayed n=77 CP-SAT command differs from the table in worker count and budget, no CaDiCaL invocation is given, and some seeds and stopping conditions are incomplete.
